atomicity.reason: Three obligations are bundled: the entry transition on first violation, the exit transition on reset, and the continuous open-command assertion while latched - the last would stand alone as a complete requirement, and the title covers only the exit transition.
atomicity.suggestion: Split the latched output behaviour ('keeps asserting the open command regardless of subsequent sample sets') into its own requirement, and align the title with whatever obligations remain in the body.

comprehensibility.reason: Both state names are quoted literally and the triggering events are named, so the requirement reads on its own.

feasibility.reason: A two-state latch with an external reset is trivially implementable and is consistent with the contactor actuator's unconditional-off behaviour while latched.

parent_fit.reason: ARCH_SAFETY_SUPERVISOR owns the two-state RUN / FAULT_LATCHED machine whose only exit is a diagnostic service reset; this requirement specifies that machine's transitions.

unambiguity.reason: 'shall transition back to RUN only on receipt of a diagnostic service reset request' states a necessary condition, leaving open whether a reset always causes the transition (e.g. while the violation still holds), and the power-up state is not stated.
unambiguity.suggestion: Separate necessity from sufficiency, e.g. 'shall transition to RUN when, and only when, a diagnostic service reset request is received', and state the state entered at initialisation.

verifiability.reason: Both states are named literally and both transitions are event-driven, so a test can drive a violation, assert FAULT_LATCHED and the held open command, then apply a reset and assert RUN.

summary: Refines the supervisor's two-state machine faithfully, but the body carries three obligations where the title claims only the exit condition, and 'only on receipt' states a necessary rather than a sufficient condition.
